programs.haiku:
"""Web and internet vocabulary, as a negative activation.

Layer-0 MLP component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:512 is silent on nearly all text. It turns
negative on the words for the internet and the web, in several languages, and on the
network and URL pieces that go with them. The strongest responses are to "web" and
"internet" themselves (" web", " Web", "-web", ".web", "internet", "Internet", Chinese
网 and 網, Russian интернет). Weaker responses come from "network", "online", "net",
"website" and Chinese compounds with 网 (网站, 网络), and from domain and URL fragments
such as ".com", "://", "www", "URL" and "blog". Compounds like "webcam" or "Weber" do not fire.

The program reads only the newest token. It strips punctuation and spaces, lowercases it,
and returns a strength by group:
    web, internet, 网, 網, интернет, ...        -6
    network, online, net, website, 网站, 网络    -2
    ://, .com, .net, www, URL, blog, .github     -1.2
Everything else predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

WEB_WORDS = {"web", "webs", "internet", "интернет", "インターネット", "互联网", "网", "網"}
NETWORK_WORDS = {"network", "networks", "online", "net", "website", "websites", "网站", "网络",
                 "在线", "网址", "官网"}
URL_PIECES = {"://", ".com", ".net", ".org", "www", "url", "blog", "blogs", ".github"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    core = word.strip(" ._-/:")
    if core in WEB_WORDS:
        value = -6.0
    elif core in NETWORK_WORDS:
        value = -2.0
    elif word in URL_PIECES or core in URL_PIECES:
        value = -1.2
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 513: a "mid-word syllable" detector.

It fires on a short piece of a word that is one consonant plus a vowel (ca, de, mo, ka,
ти, ...), especially a b/c/d/g/k/m/p/t onset, when the piece continues a word already
begun by the previous token (name and word fragments such as "Sac|ca", "Wag|ga",
"Tol|ga"). It is near zero on whole words, word-initial pieces after punctuation,
vowel-initial pieces and CJK. Stateless: it reads only the current token, the previous
token and whether they share a document. Value = shape weight x context weight.
"""

READS = ()

VOWELS = set("aeiouyаеёиоуыэюя")
STOPS = set("bcdgkmpt")

# activation (mean) by the shape of the current token
SHAPE = {
    "cv2_stop": 0.75,    # 2 letters, consonant b c d g k m p t then a vowel: "mo", "de", "ca"
    "cv2_other": 0.44,   # 2 letters, other consonant then a vowel: "ka", "ti", "ro"
    "cv2_upper": 0.31,   # same shape but capitalised: "Ca", "To"
    "cv3": 0.25,         # 3 letters with a vowel: "ten", "kin"
    "cv1_stop": 0.3,     # one stop consonant: "c", "d", "p"
    "other_cons": 0.05,  # other single letters and consonant clusters
    "vowel_start": -0.03,
    "other": 0.0,        # spaced words, digits, punctuation, CJK
}


def shape(s):
    if s.startswith(" ") or not s.isalpha():
        return "other"
    if s[0] in VOWELS:
        return "vowel_start"
    if len(s) == 2 and s[-1] in VOWELS:
        if s[0].isupper():
            return "cv2_upper"
        return "cv2_stop" if s[0] in STOPS else "cv2_other"
    if len(s) == 3 and any(c in VOWELS for c in s):
        return "cv3"
    if len(s) == 1 and s in STOPS:
        return "cv1_stop"
    return "other_cons"


def context(prev, same_doc):
    """How the piece is attached to what came before: 0 at a document start."""
    if not same_doc or not prev:
        return 0.0
    if prev.startswith(" "):
        # a new word began before: a long word counts for more than a short one
        return 0.9 if len(prev.strip()) >= 3 else 0.4
    if prev.isalpha():
        return 1.0  # mid-word: the previous piece is a fragment of this word
    return 0.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    return carry, float(SHAPE[shape(s)] * context(prev, same_doc))
programs.luna:
"""Guess higher activation for adjacent letter pieces, especially short ones."""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    position = prefix.position
    previous = ""
    if position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]

    inside_word = (
        bool(token)
        and token[0].isalpha()
        and bool(previous)
        and previous[-1].isalpha()
    )
    if inside_word and len(token) <= 2:
        return None, 0.0525
    if inside_word:
        return None, 0.015
    return None, 0.0035

programs.haiku:
r"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:514 -- the "open parenthesis starts an aside in prose" component.

What it does: this component writes a negative value when an opening parenthesis " (" (or
fullwidth "（") starts a parenthetical aside in ordinary English-like prose, e.g. "...the
community (or communities)". The size depends on what precedes the bracket:
  - after sentence-final punctuation (. ? ! ") the aside is strongest (about -0.35);
  - after a word (about -0.25); after a comma, colon or semicolon (about -0.15);
  - after anything else (digits, closing brackets, operators) only a little (about -0.05).
In code, the same bracket (e.g. "if (" or "= (") gives about 0 or slightly positive, so the
prediction is scaled down when the recent tokens look like code: the share of the last 30
tokens containing code punctuation ({ } ; = < > [ ] | & + * / \ $ # or a tab) is measured,
and the value goes to 0 once that share reaches 20%.
Everything else predicts 0. The carry holds the recent code flags and resets at each document.

Why: the largest, most consistent activations of this component are on these brackets (the
standalone " (" token alone holds about a fifth of the variance). The rest of its activity is
a diffuse spread over many ordinary words that has no simple description, so this program
does not try to predict it; a full token table would add roughly 0.1-0.15 of variance
explained but is not a concept.
"""

READS = ()

OPEN_BRACKETS = {" (", "（"}
END_PUNCTUATION = {".", "?", "!", '"', "”"}
COMMA_LIKE = {",", ":", ";"}
CODE_CHARS = set("{};=<>[]\t|&+*/\\$#")
WINDOW = 30


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    flags, doc = carry if carry is not None else ([], None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        flags = []
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if tok in OPEN_BRACKETS and len(prefix) > 1:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
        if prev in END_PUNCTUATION:
            base = -0.35
        elif prev.isalpha():
            base = -0.25
        elif prev in COMMA_LIKE:
            base = -0.15
        else:
            base = -0.05
        codeness = sum(flags) / max(1, len(flags))
        value = base * max(0.0, 1.0 - 5.0 * codeness)
    flags = (flags + [any(c in CODE_CHARS for c in tok)])[-WINDOW:]
    return (flags, doc), value
programs.luna:
"""Use a small negative pulse for tokens ending in a parenthesis opener.

High-impact harvested examples repeatedly occur at an opening parenthesis.
This lexical shortcut marks openers after a space or period; it does not try to
interpret the parenthetical text. Other positions get a near-zero baseline.
"""
READS = ()

BACKGROUND = -0.00272
OPEN_PAREN = -0.16


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token.endswith(" (") or token.endswith(".("):
        return None, OPEN_PAREN
    return None, BACKGROUND

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):

                      0.25 if previous[:1].isupper() else -0.15)

"""Layer-0 MLP unit 517 (down_proj): fires on the continuation of a split CJK character.

Qwen's tokenizer is byte-level. A non-ASCII character (most often Chinese, Japanese or
Korean) can be cut across tokens, so a token holding part of a character decodes alone to
U+FFFD (a broken fragment). This unit responds when the current token is a fragment and the
previous token was also a fragment: the model is partway through a character it has not
yet finished. Its size grows with how much CJK text came just before (last 32 tokens of the
same document): strong inside Chinese/Japanese/Korean text, weak for fragments in other
text (emoji, Latin symbols split into bytes). Elsewhere it is off.

Main program: predict 0 except on such continuation fragments, where it predicts
0.5 + 2 * (share of CJK tokens in the 32 tokens before).
"""

READS = ()

# Unicode blocks counted as CJK: Japanese kana, CJK ideographs, Hangul syllables.
CJK_RANGES = (("぀", "ヿ"), ("㐀", "鿿"), ("가", "힯"))
WINDOW = 32  # tokens of context used for the CJK share


def _is_cjk(text):
    return any(lo <= ch <= hi for ch in text for lo, hi in CJK_RANGES)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    # the current token and the one before it both decode to a broken fragment
    if "�" not in strings[-1] or "�" not in strings[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    # share of CJK tokens among the up to 32 tokens before (same document)
    recent = []
    for i in range(t - 1, max(-1, t - WINDOW - 1), -1):
        if prefix.document_ids[i] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
            break
        recent.append(strings[i])
    share = sum(_is_cjk(s) for s in recent) / max(1, len(recent))
    return None, 0.5 + 2.0 * share

"""Question-mark and ampersand detector (layers.0.mlp.down_proj, component 520).

This component is a token-identity feature that writes a strong positive signal when the
current token is a question mark or an ampersand. It is nearly silent elsewhere.
  - A bare question mark ("?", " ?", "？", "؟") gives the strongest response, about 1.4.

    gives a weaker response, about 0.55.
  - An ampersand token ("&", " &", "(&", ">&", "＆") gives about 1.0.
  - A lone " ." token, which is weakly sentence-final, gives about 0.34 (a rough, less
    reliable extra).
Everything else is 0. The activation depends only on the current token, so the program
reads no earlier context.
"""

READS = ()

QUESTION_MARKS = {"?", "？", "؟"}  # ASCII, fullwidth and Arabic question marks
AMPERSANDS = {"&", "＆"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token.strip(" ") in QUESTION_MARKS:
        value = 1.4

This component reads only the current token's text, so its value depends only on
which word fragment the token spells. It is strongest on the fragment "rec" (or "Rec",
" rec", "_rec") and on " recall" and its forms. It is medium on whole words that start
with "rec" in the sense of record / recur / recent / recipient (e.g. " record",
" recorded", " recent", " recipient", " recursion"), and weaker on other "rec-" words
(recipe, recommend, recover, recycle). It also fires a little on "rem-" words
(remember, reminder) and "prec-" words (precise, precision). Words that only look
similar but are different (receive, receipt, recess, rect-, reckless, remove,
remain) stay at 0. Context is ignored, so a token gives the same value wherever it
appears.

READS = ()

BARE_REC = 3.8       # "rec", "Rec", " rec", "_rec", "(rec"
RECALL = 4.8         # " recall", " recalling", " recalls"
RECORD_LIKE = 1.5    # " record", " records", " recorded", " recent", " recipient", " recursion"
REC_OTHER = 0.7      # other rec- words: recipe, recommend, recover, recycle
REM_PREC = 1.0       # " remember", " reminder", " precise", " precision"
ZERO_PREFIXES = ("rece", "rect", "recess", "recharg", "reck")  # receive, receipt, rectangle...


def level(text):
    word = text.strip().lower()
    stem = word.lstrip("_(.-")
    if stem == "rec":
        return BARE_REC
    if stem.startswith("recall"):
        return RECALL
    if stem.startswith(ZERO_PREFIXES):
        return 0.0
    if stem.startswith(("record", "recur", "recent", "recip", "recap", "recount")):
        return RECORD_LIKE
    if stem.startswith("rec"):
        return REC_OTHER
    if stem.startswith("remember") or stem.startswith("reminder") or stem == "remarkable":
        return REM_PREC
    if stem.startswith("preci") or stem == "prec":
        return REM_PREC

built around the letters u-r, read as a syllable at the start of the piece. It is strongest
when the whole piece is "ur" with at most one letter in front: ur, pur, cur, bur, tur,

urs, turn, sure, curve, pure). Longer words where the letters "ur" come later, or whole
common words such as "our", "your", "four", "return", "course", stay near zero, and so does

# A piece starting with that syllable and a short tail: url, ure, urs, turn, sure, curve.
UR_TAIL = re.compile("[a-z]?ur[a-z]{1,2}")

# A longer word whose first syllable is ur-like: current, surface, purpose, during, further.
LONG_UR = re.compile("[a-z]?ur[a-z]{2,}")

# Whole common words that contain "ur" but do not start with the syllable.
COMMON = {"our", "ours"}

# Mean activation of each class (training text): short piece, tail, long word, other "ur".
LEVELS = (3.7, 1.2, 0.6, 0.2)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Letters only, lower case: " Pur" and "pur" count alike.
    word = "".join(c for c in prefix.token_strings[-1].lower() if c.isalpha())
    if "ur" not in word or word in COMMON:
        return carry, 0.0
    if SHORT_UR.fullmatch(word):
        return carry, LEVELS[0]
    if UR_TAIL.fullmatch(word):
        return carry, LEVELS[1]
    if LONG_UR.fullmatch(word):

    return carry, LEVELS[3]

"""Digit-zero detector for layers.0.mlp.down_proj:527.

What it responds to: the digit 0 written inside a number, such as the last 0 of
"1960s", "400 M", "10", or a fullwidth ０ in "６，０００円". It is silent on other
tokens, and on a 0 that starts a number or follows a space, a letter or punctuation.

How strong it is depends on the digit just before the 0:
  - after 3 to 9 it is strong (about 0.85 to 1.2),
  - after 0 it is strong (about 0.95),
  - after 1 it is weaker (about 0.6),
  - after 2 it is almost silent (about 0.05): the 2 in "20", "2010", "120" suppresses it.
A 0 with two digits before it (for example "1960" or "400") is stronger by about 0.2.
Digits of any width count (ASCII or fullwidth), via their decimal value.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# How strongly a 0 fires after each decimal digit value.
STRENGTH_AFTER = {0: 0.95, 1: 0.6, 2: 0.05, 3: 0.85, 4: 1.0, 5: 1.05, 6: 1.1, 7: 1.15, 8: 1.1, 9: 1.2}
LONGER_NUMBER_BONUS = 0.2  # added when the 0 has a digit before the digit before it


def digit_value(token):
    """The decimal value of a one-character digit token (ASCII or fullwidth), else None."""
    if len(token) == 1 and token.isdecimal():
        return unicodedata.decimal(token)
    return None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if len(tokens) < 2 or docs[-2] != docs[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    if digit_value(tokens[-1]) != 0:
        return None, 0.0
    before = digit_value(tokens[-2])
    if before is None:
        return None, 0.0
    value = STRENGTH_AFTER[before]
    if len(tokens) >= 3 and docs[-3] == docs[-1] and digit_value(tokens[-3]) is not None:
        value += LONGER_NUMBER_BONUS
    return None, value

"""Give a small pulse to 0 when it continues a number-like string."""
import re

READS = ()

ZERO_PULSE = 0.7
_DECIMAL_TAIL = re.compile(r"[0-9][0-9,._]*$")
_HEX_TAIL = re.compile(r"(?:0[xX]|#)[0-9A-Fa-f]*$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Recognize a zero after digits or a simple hexadecimal prefix."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ""
    continues_number = bool(
        _DECIMAL_TAIL.search(previous) or _HEX_TAIL.search(previous)
    )
    is_zero = prefix.token_strings[-1] == "0"
    value = ZERO_PULSE if is_zero and continues_number else 0.0
    tail = (previous + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-24:]
    return (doc, tail), value

"""Sparse negative responses to school, learning, and science vocabulary.

Study characters 学/學 and Korean 학 are strongest. Their compounds and
English school/academic words are weaker. This recognizes word forms, not
whether a passage is generally about education. It also recognizes school
levels, school types, and constructions like 'School of' and 'learn to'.
'Machine learning' is weaker than other uses of 'learning'. Unrecognized
tokens return zero; the previous word is forgotten at document boundaries.
The prominent negative training peaks align with these written forms, so
this uses lexical and compound rules rather than a general topic score.

    (2.4, {'academic', 'ademic'}),
    (1.6, {'academy', 'scholar', 'scholarship', 'scholarships'}),
    (1.35, {'school', 'chool', 'university'}),
    (1.2, {'acad', 'academ', 'academia', 'academics', 'scholarly',
           'wissenschaft', 'issenschaft'}),
    (1.05, {'chemistry', 'physics', 'physicist', 'scientific',
            'scientifically', 'mathematics', 'science', 'sciences'}),
    (1.0, {'student', 'semester'}),
    (0.9, {'learning', 'students', 'schools', 'universities', 'scholars',
           'economics', 'economist', 'universität'}),
    (0.78, {'learn', 'learns', 'college', 'colleges', 'mathematical', 'maths'}),
    (0.7, {'chemical', 'psychology', 'literary', 'institute', 'schul'}),
    (0.6, {'learned', 'learner', 'learners', 'professor', 'professors',
           'chem', 'freshman', 'biology', 'literature'}),
    (0.5, {'scientist', 'scientists', 'scient', 'mathematic'}),
    (0.4, {'pupils', 'pupil', 'campus', 'graduate', 'homework', 'educational'}),
    (0.3, {'ological', 'ology', 'ologists'}),
    (1.3, {'наук', 'учеб'}),
    (0.9, {'науч', 'школ', 'школь', 'schüler'}),
)


def strength(raw):
    token = raw.strip()
    word = token.casefold().lstrip('._-/@')
    if token in {'学', '學', '학'}:
        return {'学': 7.65, '學': 7.25, '학': 5.0}[token]
    # Normalize the traditional forms of 'study' and 'practice'.
    c = token.replace('學', '学').replace('習', '习')
    if '学' in c:
        if c == '大学生':
            return 0.85
        if len(c) > 3:
            return 1.0
        if '学生' in c or '教学' in c or c in {'同学们', '学员', '学历'}:
            return 1.5
        if '学校' in c:
            return 1.7
        if '学习' in c or c in {'同学', '数学', '科学', '哲学', '学位', '学科'}:
            return 2.2
        if c in {'上学', '入学', '经济学', '物理学', '法学'}:
            return 4.4
        if c.endswith('学') or c in {'学院', '学术', '学者', '学会', '学子'}:
            return 3.2
        return 2.0
    if token in {'학교', '학생', '대학'}:
        return 2.2
    if word in {'học', 'ọc'}:
        return 3.2 if word == 'học' else 2.0
    if word == 'math':
        return 0.56 if raw.startswith(' ') and token.islower() else 0.32
    if word == 'univers':
        return 0.4 if token[:1].isupper() else 0.0
    for amount, words in EDUCATION_WORDS:
        if word in words:
            if word in {'student', 'students', 'school'} and token[:1].isupper():

    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip().casefold().lstrip('._-/@')
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    same_document = carry is not None and carry[0] == document
    previous = carry[1] if same_document else ''
    value = -strength(raw)
    if '\ufffd' in raw and same_document:
        # A byte fragment may complete a recognizable study character.
        last = prefix.text_prefixes[-1][-1:]
        value = {'学': -9.0, '學': -5.2, '학': -6.3}.get(last, value)
    if raw.strip() == 'learning':
        value = -1.03
    if word == 'learning' and previous == 'machine':
        value = -0.3
    elif word == 'school':
        levels = {'high': 1.0, 'middle': 0.8, 'elementary': 0.8,
                  'secondary': 1.0, 'graduate': 1.1}
        if previous in levels:
            value = -levels[previous]
            if raw.strip()[:1].isupper():
                value -= 0.15
        elif previous in {'law', 'business', 'sunday'}:
            value = -2.1
        elif previous == 'the':
            value = -1.6
    elif word == 'of':
        value = {'school': -0.37, 'university': -0.14, 'academy': -0.19,
                 'student': -0.56, 'students': -0.59, 'learning': -0.7}.get(
                     previous, value)
    elif word in {'to', 'the', 'a', 'about'} and previous in {'learn', 'learning'}:
        value = -0.35 if previous == 'learning' else -0.25
    return (document, word), value

    context = min(1.0, context * 0.99 + EVIDENCE[kind])
    return (document, context, word), float(value)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:529 - a "physics vocabulary" component.

This component is mostly negative. It goes strongly negative on the words of quantum
many-body, solid-state and scattering physics (electron, phonon, lattice, spin, quantum,
momentum, scattering, excitation, ...), more weakly on general physics and materials words
(energy, particle, photon, atom, emission, ...), and only slightly on generic technical
words (number, layer, plane, function, ...). Everything else is about zero.

The response is stronger when the text has recently been physics-heavy: the program keeps a
decaying count of physics words within the current document and scales its predictions up
with it. It resets at each document boundary.

Tiers are judged by eye from activations on training text. The word lists are a
hand-written proxy for what the layer-0 MLP responds to; they capture only a small share of
the variance, because many rare technical words each carry a small, idiosyncratic value.

    "fluctuations", "collision", "collisions", "nucleus", "nuclei", "ion", "ions", "exciton",
    "excitons", "excitation", "excitations", "excited", "triplet", "fermi", "eigen", "hamiltonian",
    "bulk", "anomalous", "longitudinal", "plasmon", "magnon", "boson", "fermion",
}
# General physics and materials terms: weaker responses.
MEDIUM = {
    "energy", "energies", "particle", "particles", "photon", "photons", "atom", "atoms", "atomic",
    "emission", "entropy", "kinetic", "tunnel", "tunneling", "diffusion", "thermal", "crystal",
    "plasma", "laser", "correlation", "correlations", "transition", "transitions", "charge",
    "charges", "electric", "magnetic", "absorption", "susceptibility", "polarization", "proton",
    "neutron", "coupling", "interaction", "interactions", "doping", "lifetime", "bose",
    "dispersion", "photoelectric", "superconductor", "superconducting", "conductivity",
}
# Generic technical words: a faint response.
WEAK = {
    "number", "total", "single", "pair", "few", "many", "two", "three", "layer", "layers",
    "plane", "system", "systems", "function", "functions", "section", "state", "states", "level",
    "temperature", "gas", "region", "spatial", "statistical", "binding", "order", "critical",
    "optical", "cavity", "mode", "modes", "molecule", "molecules", "density", "field", "fields",
    "effective", "classical", "finite", "local", "along", "free", "long",
}

DECAY = 0.98  # how fast the physics-heaviness of the text fades, per token
BOOST = 0.1   # extra scale per unit of recent physics-word count


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict this token's activation from its own word and the text before it."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()

"""Approximate transfer/motion argument markers using familiar word classes.

Predict negative activations on 'sent to', 'received from', 'passed through';
'provided with' and 'come with' are positive. Eight broad word families share
response estimates. A recent cue can precede a short object phrase; distance
and split-word penalties weaken it. 'Want/need to' is treated as infinitival,
not transfer. This is a lexical heuristic, not a full grammar parser.

Small additional rules cover Chinese 给/給, 'give rise', 'give up', 'supply
chain', and Malay/Indonesian 'kepada' (to). Unhandled tokens predict zero.
The sixteen-token history resets at each document boundary. Finer differences
within verb families and most weak background responses are omitted.
"""
import re

READS = ()
PREPS = ('to', 'from', 'with', 'by', 'through', 'into')
# Responses in PREPS order, for familiar semantic word families.
CUES = (
    # Giving, allocating, paying, and communicating.
    ('give grant donate assign distribute allocate award credit entrust '
     'submit communicate administer issue offer present pay sell lend yield '
     'appoint report write',
     (-2.17, -0.84, 0.34, -0.57, -1.0, -0.37)),
    # Sending and transferring.
    ('send mail transmit deliver hand forward email dispatch pass transfer',
     (-3.24, -1.64, 0.33, -0.67, -1.59, -2.09)),
    # Provision, reception, acquisition, motion, arrival, availability.
    ('provide supply furnish',
     (-2.44, -1.17, 1.53, -1.42, -1.2, 0.03)),
    ('receive',
     (-1.14, -1.86, 0.42, -0.97, -1.24, -0.68)),
    ('accept collect obtain acquire import export download',
     (-0.86, -0.65, 0.07, -0.37, -0.77, -0.35)),
    ('go return flow stream feed pour inject input output travel transport '
     'convey',
     (-1.49, -1.02, 0.31, -0.52, -1.12, -1.2)),
    ('come',
     (-0.34, -1.09, 1.03, -0.03, -0.66, -0.27)),
    ('available accessible obtainable downloadable payable owe attribute '
     'attributable',
     (-1.82, -1.32, 0.49, -0.6, -1.3, -0.1)),
)
FAMILY = {w: i for i, (words, _) in enumerate(CUES) for w in words.split()}
CONTROL = set('want need try attempt seem tend allow expect have able unable possible '
              'likely ready necessary'.split())
OBJECTS = set('message signal data information feedback result mail email letter money '
              'fund payment refund gift power energy current water air gas fluid copy '
              'file parameter argument value object code award support good product '
              'property service packet benefit sample resource advice answer dollar '
              'income revenue funding donation transmission passage debt aid'.split())
ROOTS = set(FAMILY) | CONTROL | OBJECTS
IRREGULAR = dict(gave='give', given='give', sent='send', sold='sell', paid='pay',
                 lent='lend', went='go', gone='go', came='come', fed='feed',
                 had='have', wrote='write', written='write')
PRONOUNS = set('it them us him her me you'.split())
BOUNDARIES = set('in on at for to from with by into through and or but as than'.split())
DETERMINERS = set('a an the this that these those my your his her its '
                  'our their'.split())


def root(word):
    """Normalize familiar English inflections only."""
    if word in IRREGULAR:
        return IRREGULAR[word]
    if word in ROOTS:
        return word
    for ending in ('ing', 'ed', 'es', 's'):
        if word.endswith(ending):
            stem = word[:-len(ending)]
            candidates = [stem, stem+'e']
            if len(stem) > 1 and stem[-1] == stem[-2]:
                candidates.append(stem[:-1])
            if stem.endswith('i'):
                candidates.append(stem[:-1]+'y')
            for candidate in candidates:
                if candidate in ROOTS:
                    return candidate
    return word


def describe(history):
    """Find a recent cue and describe the intervening phrase."""
    words = re.findall(r'[A-Za-z]+|[0-9]+|[^\w\s]', ''.join(history))[-12:]
    words = [w.lower() for w in words]
    head = root(words[-1]) if words else ''
    for gap, word in enumerate(reversed(words)):
        lemma = root(word)
        if word in '.!?;' or word in BOUNDARIES:
            break
        family = FAMILY.get(lemma)
        # Bare hand/hands and forward are often nouns or directions.
        if family is not None and word not in {'hand', 'hands', 'forward'}:
            before = words[-gap-2] if len(words)>gap+1 else ''
            if (word in {'supply', 'return', 'offer', 'present', 'pay', 'pass'}
                    and before in DETERMINERS):
                continue
            if gap and family == FAMILY['available']:
                continue
            split = word not in re.findall('[A-Za-z]+', ' '.join(history).lower())
            return family, gap, head, split
        if gap == 0 and (head in CONTROL or word.endswith(('ed', 'ing'))):
            break
    return None, 0, head, False


BASE = (-0.1, -0.13, 0.03, -0.01, -0.37, -0.12)
# Columns: ordinary phrase, personal pronoun, exchanged thing.
LOOKBACK = (
    (0.5, 0.85, 0.86),
    (0.35, 0.49, 1.0),
    (0.9, 1.26, 0.77),
    (0.2, 0.75, 0.44),
    (0.76, 0.91, 1.09),
    (0.63, 0.75, 0.91),
)
SPLIT_SCALE = (0.49, 0.6, 0.25, 0.55, 0.65, 0.72)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = [] if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower().lstrip('_-')
    value = 0.0
    if word in PREPS:
        j = PREPS.index(word)
        family, gap, head, split = describe(history)
        value = BASE[j]
        if family is not None:
            value = CUES[family][1][j]
            if (head == 'go' and history
                    and history[-1].strip().lower() == 'going'):
                value *= 0.5
            if gap:
                # Ordinary phrase, personal pronoun, or exchanged thing.
                kind = 1 if head in PRONOUNS else 2 if head in OBJECTS else 0
                value *= LOOKBACK[j][kind] * max(0.3, 1-0.07*(gap-1))
            if split:
                value *= SPLIT_SCALE[j]
        elif word == 'to':
            if head in CONTROL:
                value = 0.0
            elif head in {'due', 'thanks'}:
                value = -0.8
            elif head in {'is', 'are', 'used', 'way', 'related', 'close', 'prior'}:
                value = 0.2
            elif head in OBJECTS:
                value = -0.9
        elif word == 'from' and head in OBJECTS:
            value = -0.9
        elif word == 'by' and head.endswith('ed'):
            value = -0.23
    elif '给' in token or '給' in token:
        recent = ''.join(history)[-10:]+token
        # Send, hand over, transmit, grant, or sell.
        sending = any(c in recent for c in '发送交递遞輸输賦赋卖賣')
        value = -3.3 if sending else -1.4
        # Fused recipient pronouns and other common continuations weaken it.
        if any(c in token for c in '我你他她您们們出予力'):
            value *= 0.4
    elif word in {'rise', 'up', 'chain', 'chains'} and history:
        previous = root(history[-1].strip().lower())
        if previous == 'give' and word in {'rise', 'up'}:
            value = 1.5 if word == 'rise' else 0.9
        elif previous == 'supply' and word in {'chain', 'chains'}:
            value = 1.4
    elif word == 'kepada':
        value = -1.0
    return (doc, (history+[token])[-16:]), float(value)

"""Predict capitalized identifier starts in programming-like text.

Recent programming keywords and punctuation provide a fading code-context
score. Capitalized names after declarations, dots, brackets and expression
separators get larger values; CamelCase continuations and ordinary prose get
less. Single letters and two-letter fragments are discounted. All-capital
text is much weaker. The lowercase constructor keyword `new` gets a negative
prediction in strong code context.
"""
import re

READS = ()
CODE_WORDS = set('''
new class struct enum interface extends implements instanceof public private
protected static final abstract virtual override namespace using import
package from fn func function def let const var val void bool int float
double char string return throw throws raise try catch except elif null nil
true false none self this impl template typename typedef extern async await
export isinstance theorem lemma axiom inductive structure module
noncomputable variable variables
'''.split())
DECLARATIONS = set('''
new class struct enum interface extends implements instanceof import
namespace using throw throws raise typedef typename impl for return public
private protected static final abstract override virtual void bool int float
double char string def fn func function type const module theorem lemma
axiom structure inductive mut
'''.split())
# (response outside code, response in strong code context)
LEVELS = {
    'declaration': (0.21, 2.52),
    'member': (0.45, 1.29),
    'bracket': (0.37, 1.65),
    'expression': (0.15, 1.75),
    'compound': (0.08, 0.25),
    'whitespace': (0.02, 1.21),
    'indented': (0.17, 1.17),
    'ordinary': (0.00, 0.53),
}


def last_word(text):
    match = re.search(r'([A-Za-z]+)$', text.rstrip())
    return match.group(1) if match else ''


def indentation(text):
    text = text.expandtabs(4)
    return len(text) - len(text.lstrip())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0.0, 0, True, '')
    _, code, margin, at_margin, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if at_margin:
        margin += indentation(token)
        at_margin = token.isspace()
    strength = max(code - 0.5, 0)
    confidence = strength / (strength + 3)
    text = token.lstrip()
    match = re.search('[A-Za-z]', text)
    lead = text[:match.start()] if match else text
    word = text[match.start():] if match else ''
    letters = ''.join(c for c in word if c.isalpha())
    capital = (bool(word) and word[0].isupper()
               and not any(c.isalnum() for c in lead))
    title = capital and (len(letters) == 1 or not letters.isupper())
    value = -0.002
    if title:
        if last_word(previous) in DECLARATIONS:
            category = 'declaration'
        elif '.' in lead:
            category = 'member'
        elif (any(c in lead for c in '(<[')
              or previous.endswith(('(', '<', '['))):
            category = 'bracket'
        elif previous.rstrip().endswith(('=', '->', '::', ':=', ',', ':')):
            category = 'expression'
        elif not token[:1].isspace() and previous[-1:].isalnum():
            category = 'compound'
        elif previous[-1:].isspace():
            category = 'whitespace'
        elif margin >= 2:
            category = 'indented'
        else:
            category = 'ordinary'
        low, high = LEVELS[category]
        size = (0.4 if len(letters) == 1
                else 0.7 if len(letters) == 2 else 1.0)
        value = size * (low + confidence * (high - low))
    elif capital:
        value = 0.003 + confidence * (
            0.47 - 0.37 * previous[-1:].isupper())
    elif last_word(token) == 'new':
        value = 0.13 - 0.72 * confidence

    evidence = min(3, sum(token.count(c) for c in ';{}=')
                   + 2 * token.count('::'))
    evidence += last_word(token) in CODE_WORDS
    code = 0.97 * code + evidence
    if '\n' in token:
        tail = token.rsplit('\n', 1)[-1]
        margin, at_margin = indentation(tail), not tail or tail.isspace()
    return (doc, code, margin, at_margin, token), float(value)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:536 -- a "type/class name in source code" detector.

What it does: the component fires on capitalised programming identifiers (type,
class, enum and library names such as List, Result, Vec, Self, Wallet, Integer,
KeyCode, Test) when they sit inside code rather than prose. It is strongest right
after code syntax (`new Wallet`, `public Task`, `import Foo`, `x = Foo`, `<Item`,
`::Vec`) and weaker on all-caps constants (ACC, KEY) and on capitalised English
words (The, It, I), which it ignores.

How this program predicts it: for each token that is a capitalised word
(optionally led by a space, '(', '.', '<' or '['), the prediction is the
"code density" of the last 64 tokens in the same document (the share of recent
tokens that look like code: brackets, operators, indentation, keywords), doubled
if the previous token is a code cue (new, public, import, =, <, ::, ...),
x1.5 if the token starts with a space, and halved if it is all capitals.
Every other token predicts 0.
"""
import re

READS = ()

NAME = re.compile(r"[ (.\[<\t]*[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
CODE_CUES = {"new", "public", "private", "import", "return", "class", "static",
             "=", "<", "::", ":", "->", "(", ",", "{"}
CODE_LIKE = re.compile(r".*[{}();=<>\[\]:\t\n].*|\s{2,}.*|.*(::|->|\.\w).*", re.S)
KEYWORDS = {"new", "public", "private", "protected", "import", "return", "class",
            "static", "void", "int", "string", "null", "true", "false", "if", "else",
            "for", "while", "let", "var", "const", "def", "fn", "func", "use"}
WINDOW = 64


def is_code_token(s):
    """True for a token that looks like source code rather than prose."""
    return s.strip() in KEYWORDS or CODE_LIKE.fullmatch(s) is not None


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: flags (is_code) of the previous WINDOW tokens of this document
    flags = list(carry or [])
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        flags = []
        prev = ""
    density = sum(flags) / len(flags) if flags else 0.0
    value = 0.0
    if NAME.fullmatch(s):
        value = density
        if prev.strip() in CODE_CUES or prev in CODE_CUES:
            value *= 2.0
        if s[:1] == " ":
            value *= 1.5
        if s.strip().isupper():
            value *= 0.5
    flags = (flags + [is_code_token(s)])[-WINDOW:]
    return flags, value

What it does: it switches on for a few kinds of word, and mostly for the subject
and possessive pronouns, quantifiers and "is/be/and/of" when they are glued to the
previous piece of text (no leading space). Most other positions sit near zero.

Rules, from the strength it shows in the data (about 0.1 to 0.7):
  * Pronouns after a space: "they"/"They" (strongest), "their", "them", "he",
    "She", "we".
  * Quantifiers after a space: "all", "All", "over".
  * "The" mid-sentence (after a word or comma, not after a full stop or line break).
  * Common words with no leading space (e.g. after a hyphen, a line break, or inside
    a split word): "and", "is", "be", "of", "to", "the", "its", "her", "we", "he",
    "all", "over", "they".
  * Everything else, including sentence-initial "The" and " and"/" is" with a
    leading space, predicts 0.

This is a word list, not a full model of the component: it explains about a fifth
of the variance. Context effects on "the" and "of" are left out.
"""

READS = ()

# Words after a space: pronouns and quantifiers, with their typical activation.
SPACED = {
    " they": 0.6, " They": 0.7, " their": 0.3, " them": 0.2,
    " he": 0.13, " He": 0.26, " she": 0.25, " She": 0.37,
    " we": 0.07, " We": 0.16,
    " all": 0.3, " All": 0.47, " over": 0.43,
    " As": 0.25, " Of": 0.25, " And": 0.17,
}
# Common words glued to the previous piece (no leading space).
GLUED = {
    "and": 0.5, "is": 0.4, "be": 0.5, "of": 0.5, "to": 0.3, "the": 0.25, "its": 0.3,
    "her": 0.3, "we": 0.5, "he": 0.35, "all": 0.45, "over": 0.45, "they": 0.6,
}
# What ends a sentence or a line, so the next "The" starts one.
SENTENCE_END = {".", "!", "?", "\n", "\n\n", "<|endoftext|>", ""}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token, from that token and the one before it."""
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    if word in SPACED:
        return None, SPACED[word]
    if word == " The" and before.strip() not in SENTENCE_END:
        return None, 0.4
    if word in GLUED:
        return None, GLUED[word]
    return None, 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP down_proj component 546: the second half of a split Chinese/Japanese word.

What it responds to: a CJK character that completes a two-character word, i.e. a character
written right after another CJK character, or right after a split-up byte fragment of a
character (the tokenizer cuts some characters into byte pieces that show as U+FFFD), in
the same document. Strong examples, with the first character in brackets: 关[系], 状[态],
类[型], 战[略], 垃[圾], 环[境], 基[础], 训[练], 对[象], 广[告], 动[画], 问[题].

Strength depends on the character:
  * a character that usually ends a two-character word (系 态 略 报 司 果 象 型 题 法 ...)
    gets the full value;
  * a character that usually stands alone or starts a word (的 和 在 是 了 中 大 小 我 你 ...)
    gets none;
  * any other character gets a small value.
A Korean syllable after a non-Korean character gets a medium value, and a Korean syllable
after another Korean syllable a small one. Everything else (English, digits, punctuation,
spaces) is predicted as 0. The component fires rarely and only on CJK text, so most positions
are 0.

The magnitudes and character lists were drafted from a sample of training text (the positions
where the component was most active), and checked on other training rows. They are not fitted
to eval rows. The English word-piece pattern (Hy|brid, basket|ball) is real but not predictable
with simple rules, so it is left out.
"""

import unicodedata

# Characters that usually complete a two-character word (the second character of 活动, 关系 ...).
WORD_END = set(
    "动動画畫施约約券典格设設训訓许許合谈談达達题題法真入化导導量利型想视視座意力"
    "记記社率所客线線取进進样樣场場信当當称稱建民用集却度事体體生位片行机機伤傷"
    "色出而相语語系态態略报報司果史象胞缩縮造理键鍵息忆憶计計况況际際频頻容学學"
    "闻聞应應制性构構组組织織统統验驗务務业業品类類程件案质質数數据據段期感论論"
    "护護险險备備决決策证證府讲講运運习習"
)
# Common characters that stand alone or start a word, rarely the second half of one.
STANDALONE = set(
    "的和在是了中大小高我你他来來后後等说說三二以之内內部及做包跟特么"
    "人上到一有不会地天日与为下被着也就要都很这那个对去能可好无水月山花"
)

FULL = 0.30               # Han after Han, a word-ending character
PLAIN = 0.09              # Han after Han, any other character
FRAGMENT_FULL = 0.85      # Han completing a split byte fragment, word-ending character
FRAGMENT_PLAIN = 0.45     # Han completing a split byte fragment, any other character
HAN_TO_FRAGMENT = 0.27    # a split byte fragment right after a Han character
HANGUL_AFTER_OTHER = 0.23
HANGUL_AFTER_HANGUL = 0.09

READS = ()


def _script(token):
    """'han', 'hangul', 'fragment' or '' for one token's decoded text."""
    if token and set(token) == {"�"}:
        return "fragment"
    if len(token) != 1:
        return ""
    name = unicodedata.name(token, "")
    if "CJK" in name:
        return "han"
    if "HANGUL" in name:
        return "hangul"
    return ""


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    a, b = _script(cur), _script(prev)
    value = 0.0
    if a == "han" and b == "han":
        if cur in WORD_END:
            value = FULL
        elif cur in STANDALONE:
            value = 0.0
        else:
            value = PLAIN
    elif a == "han" and b == "fragment":
        value = FRAGMENT_FULL if cur in WORD_END else FRAGMENT_PLAIN
    elif a == "fragment" and b == "han":
        value = HAN_TO_FRAGMENT
    elif a == "hangul":
        value = HANGUL_AFTER_HANGUL if b == "hangul" else HANGUL_AFTER_OTHER
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection, component 547: a "9 inside a number" detector.

The component writes a strong negative value into the residual stream whenever the
token is the digit 9 and it continues a number, i.e. the previous token is a digit.
The size depends on that previous digit: after 2-8 it is strongest (about -0.6), after
0, 1 or 9 it is a bit weaker (about -0.43). A 9 after a decimal point or comma is
weaker still, and a 9 after a space or other symbol is weak. Every other token, and
a 9 starting a new document, gives 0. Other digits do not move it.

SMALL_PREV_DIGITS = set("019")
SEPARATORS = set(".,")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    now = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if now != "9" or len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if prev in BIG_PREV_DIGITS:
        value = -0.6
    elif prev in SMALL_PREV_DIGITS:
        value = -0.43
    elif prev in SEPARATORS:
        value = -0.3
    elif prev == " ":
        value = -0.12
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:548 — "a past-tense verb that has just been given a subject".

What it does
    This component writes a negative signal into the residual stream on finite past-tense
    main verbs in narrative text: "he [made] ...", "I [found] ...", "it [became] ...",
    "Richardson [won] ...", "the company [stated] ...". The more clearly the verb follows
    a subject, the more negative it is. It is near zero everywhere else, including
    passives and copulas ("was [made]", "is [found]", "been [used]"), infinitives and
    imperatives ("to [set]", "[Let] me"), and words after a determiner or preposition.

How the program approximates it
    1. A token counts as a past-tense verb if it is a word with a leading space that is
       either a common irregular past (said, made, went, found, ...) or ends in -ed
       (stated, featured, ...), minus a few -ed words that are not verbs (named, based, ...).
    2. Look at the previous word:
       - nothing, punctuation, a determiner, a copula/auxiliary, a preposition or "to",
         or a negation: the verb is not a finite past after a subject -> 0.
       - a subject pronoun (I, he, she, it, they, we, who, which, you) or a capitalised
         word (a name, or a sentence-initial noun): strongest, -2.0.
       - has / have / had: weak, -0.5 (perfect participles).
       - anything else (a conjunction, a comma, an adverb, a common noun): -1.0.

What the simple version gets and what it leaves out
    On 512 training rows (262k tokens) it explains about 53% of the variance and has
    r = 0.73 with the real activation; on the eval rows it scores variance explained 0.525,
    r 0.727, and substituting it for the component keeps about 54% of the KL change that
    switching the component off causes, with cross entropy slightly better than the
    unedited model. What it omits: the fine-grained size of each verb's activation
    (a per-verb lookup would add some, but token identity alone explains only about a
    third of the variance), the many -ed or verb-like words it does not recognise
    (e.g. subword pieces like "ed" in "claw ed"), and nuance in which subject types
    give the strongest response.
    """
READS = ()

IRREGULAR_PAST = frozenset("""
became began brought built bought came did drew drove fell felt flew forgot got gave
grew had held hit kept knew laid led left lost made meant met paid ran rode rose said
sat saw sent shot shook shut sang sank slept spent spoke stood stole struck taught told
thought threw understood went won wore wrote took found sold fought heard ate broke
drank beat quit chose arose sought tore
""".split())
# -ed words that are usually adjectives, nouns or present-tense forms, not past verbs
NOT_VERB = frozenset("need feed bed red seed shed speed hundred named based related sled bred led".split())
# words before which the verb is a passive/participle, copula, imperative or non-subject use
BLOCK = frozenset("""is are was were be been being am a an the of in with for as to not
will would can could may might must do does did than . : ; |""".split())
SUBJECT = frozenset("I he she it they we who which you".split())
HAVE = frozenset("has have had".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    w = tok.strip()
    if not (tok.startswith(" ") and w.isalpha()):
        return carry, 0.0
    is_past = w in IRREGULAR_PAST or (w.endswith("ed") and len(w) > 3 and w not in NOT_VERB)
    if not is_past or len(prefix.token_strings) < 2:
        return carry, 0.0
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if before == "" or before.lower() in BLOCK:
        return carry, 0.0
    if before in SUBJECT or before[:1].isupper():
        return carry, -2.0
    if before.lower() in HAVE:
        return carry, -0.5
    return carry, -1.0

programs.sol:
"""A lexical 'under' detector, with weaker relational-preposition responses.

The negative response is strongest for the token 'under', including capitals.
Code-separated 'under' and a few under-like fragments respond too.
License phrases amplify the response; 'fall/fit/proceed under' weaken it.
It also responds to under- compounds and several spatial/temporal prepositions.
For 'to', the response depends on the preceding word: compliance, causation,
response, and belonging phrases are negative, unlike ordinary infinitives.
The response continues weakly into an immediately following article.
A short text tail keeps that preceding word across token boundaries; it resets
at document boundaries. All other tokens receive zero.
"""
import re

READS = ()

# Spatial/temporal relations and translations of 'under'.
RELATIONS = {
    'into': -0.80,
    'during': -1.05,
    'within': -0.48,
    'inside': -0.76,
    'behind': -0.82,
    'upon': -0.51,
    'onto': -0.35,
    'across': -0.18,
    'against': -0.25,
    'outside': -0.37,
    'beneath': -1.32,
    'pursuant': -1.03,
    'unter': -1.10,
    'sous': -1.23,
    'bajo': -2.10,
    'sotto': -0.71,
    'под': -0.68,
}

# Under- compounds and partial compound prefixes respond more weakly.
UNDER_COMPOUNDS = {
    'underlying': -1.86,
    'underneath': -1.97,
    'underside': -2.83,
    'undergo': -1.76,
    'undergoing': -2.07,
    'undergone': -1.20,
    'underwent': -1.39,
    'underwater': -1.50,
    'underwear': -2.25,
    'underground': -0.43,
    'underscore': -0.74,
    'undergraduate': -0.98,
    'understood': -0.64,
    'undert': -3.10,
    'unders': -3.00,
    'underst': -3.35,
}


def to_response(word):
    if word in {'subject', 'subjected', 'pursuant'}:
        return -1.45
    if word in {'according', 'due', 'owing', 'thanks', 'attributed',
                'attributable'}:
        return -0.85
    if word.startswith(('respond', 'response', 'belong')):
        return -0.74
    if word.startswith(('expos', 'subscrib')) or word == 'devoted':
        return -0.60
    if word in {'assigned', 'entitled', 'entitlement', 'resistance'}:
        return -0.48
    if word == 'up':
        return -0.41
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    tail = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    previous = re.search(r'(\w+)\s*$', tail)
    previous_text = previous[1] if previous else ''
    previous = previous_text.lower()
    value = 0.0
    if word.lstrip('._-') == 'under':
        value = -7.35 if token[:1].isspace() or token[:1].isupper() else -6.83
        if word.startswith('_'):
            value = -5.6
        elif word.startswith(('.', '-')):
            value = -7.35
        elif previous == 'licensed':
            value = -11.5 if previous_text[0].isupper() else -9.6
        elif previous == 'distributed':
            value = -8.5
        elif previous in {'fall', 'falls', 'fit', 'fits', 'proceed', 'proceeding'}:
            value = -5.9
        elif not token[:1].isspace() and previous in {'w', 'as'}:
            value = -5.6
        elif not token[:1].isspace() and previous in {'bl', 'k'}:
            value = -4.1
    elif word == 'nder':
        joined = previous + word
        if joined.endswith('under'):
            value = -3.5
        elif joined.endswith('launder'):
            value = -2.25
        elif joined.endswith(('ander', 'ender')):
            value = -1.25
    elif word in UNDER_COMPOUNDS:
        value = UNDER_COMPOUNDS[word]
    elif word.startswith('under'):
        value = -0.15 if word.startswith('understand') else -1.15
    elif word == 'und':
        value = -0.20 if token[:1].isspace() and token.strip().islower() else -0.60
        if token.strip()[0].isupper():
            value = -0.75
    elif word == 'unde':
        value = -2.0 if token[:1].isspace() else -0.35
    elif word in RELATIONS:
        value = RELATIONS[word]
        if word == 'into' and (not token[:1].isspace() or token.strip()[0].isupper()):
            value = -0.63
        elif word == 'during' and token.strip()[0].isupper():
            value = -0.78
        elif word == 'unter' and not token[:1].isspace():
            value = -0.41
    elif word in {'the', 'a', 'an'}:
        strength = (-7.35 if previous == 'under' else
                    UNDER_COMPOUNDS.get(previous, RELATIONS.get(previous, 0.0)))
        value = strength * (0.15 if word == 'the' else 0.10)
    elif word in {'this', 'that', 'its', 'any'} and previous == 'under':
        value = -0.45
    elif word == 'to' and (token[:1].isspace() or tail[-1:].isspace()):
        value = to_response(previous)
    return (doc, (tail + token)[-80:]), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP output feature 549 (down_proj): a lexical "under" detector.

What it does: the component goes strongly negative on the word "under" (any
capitalisation, with or without a leading space), more weakly negative on any
other word beginning with "under" (e.g. "underlying", "undergo", "undertake"
fragments), and more weakly still on a handful of other words that take the same
kind of position in a sentence:
spatial and time prepositions ("into", "during", "behind", "inside", "within",
"upon"), "under"-words and their translations ("underneath", "undergo",
"sous", "unter", "bajo", "под"), and "to" after words that take "to" in
the sense of "according to / due to / subject to / pursuant to". It also gives a
weak negative to the article right after "under" ("under the").
Everything else is predicted as 0, which is where the component sits almost all
the time (it fires on about 0.3% of tokens).

Why: this is a token-level feature, mostly keyed to the surface word, so a word
list is the honest description. The values are the average activation for each
word in a 1024-row sample of training text.
"""

READS = ()

# Activation (negative = the component's contribution points against its usual direction)
# for the word itself, averaged over the training sample.
WORD_VALUE = {
    "under": -7.3,
    "underneath": -2.0,
    "underlying": -1.9,
    "undergo": -1.7,
    "undergoing": -1.7,
    "underwent": -1.4,
    "underwater": -1.5,
    "beneath": -1.4,
    "bajo": -2.2,
    "sous": -1.2,
    "unter": -1.1,
    "под": -0.7,
    "during": -1.0,
    "pursuant": -1.0,
    "into": -0.8,
    "behind": -0.8,
    "inside": -0.75,
    "upon": -0.5,
    "within": -0.5,
    "onto": -0.4,
}

# Words after which "to" means "according to / due to / subject to".
TO_AFTER = {
    "according", "due", "subject", "subjected", "pursuant", "owing", "thanks",
    "belong", "belongs", "belonging", "response", "respond", "responds",
    "responded", "responses", "attributed", "assigned", "exposed", "exposure",
    "entitled", "susceptible", "vulnerable",
}
TO_VALUE = -0.9
THE_AFTER_UNDER = -1.0


def _word(s):
    return s.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = _word(prefix.token_strings[-2]) if same_doc else ""
    if word in WORD_VALUE:
        value = WORD_VALUE[word]
    elif word.startswith("under"):
        value = -1.0
    elif word == "to" and prev in TO_AFTER:
        value = TO_VALUE
    elif word == "the" and prev == "under":
        value = THE_AFTER_UNDER
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Use a cautious cue for words that express location, duration, or direction.

“under”, and “during”. Such words alone do not determine the response, so this
predicts only a small negative value and leaves context-sensitive exceptions out.
"""
READS = ()

RELATIONAL_WORDS = frozenset("""
to into under during behind inside amid upon within through over
""".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return None, -0.08 if word in RELATIONAL_WORDS else 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP unit 550 (down_proj): a weak detector for capitalized words.

follows another token in the same document, e.g. the surname in "Derrick Henry" or
"Perkins" in "Mitchell B. Perkins". Everything else is predicted as 0. The unit's
large negative values are on proper names, but most name tokens are not that
strong, so a constant on capitalized words explains only a few percent of variance.
"""

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    if cur.startswith(" ") and cur[1:2].isupper():
        return None, -0.15
    return None, 0.0

"""A text cue for entity-like capitalized words.

Capitalized words in prose are predicted more negatively than ordinary words,
especially just after a preposition or article. Sentence and line starts get a
weaker response. This is a broad capitalization heuristic, not a name lookup.
"""
import re

READS = ()

_NAME_CUES = frozenset((
    "in", "of", "to", "from", "by", "with", "at", "and", "or",
    "the", "a", "an", "for", "on", "into", "across", "near",
    "around", "through", "between", "after", "before", "over",
    "under", "about", "upon", "without", "within", "mr", "mrs",
    "ms", "dr", "prof", "st",
))
_PREVIOUS_WORD = re.compile(r"([\w]+)[^\w]*$", re.UNICODE)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        sentence_start, tail = True, ""
    else:
        sentence_start, tail = carry[1], carry[2]

    word = token.lstrip()
    title_word = bool(
        word and word[0].isupper()
        and any(char.islower() for char in word[1:])
    )

    previous_match = _PREVIOUS_WORD.search(tail)
    previous_word = previous_match.group(1).lower() if previous_match else ""

    value = 0.0
    if title_word:
        if previous_word in _NAME_CUES and not tail[-1:].isspace():
            value = -0.46
        elif sentence_start:
            value = -0.08
        elif tail and tail[-1].isspace():
            value = -0.05

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:551, a diffuse, mostly token-specific feature, written as a short word-level sketch.

What it does, per token (only the current token is read):
- Chinese/Japanese Han characters: a small negative value (about -0.03). Across the corpus
  these characters are, on average, pushed down, though individual characters vary a lot
  (some near +0.3, some near -0.3).
- Degree and universality words (always, ever, once, everything, everyone, anything, thing,
  maximum, minimum, possible, impossible, highly, extremely, easily, variety, double, free,
  less): clearly negative, about -0.1.
- A few mildly positive English words (again, simply, quite, various, full, least, while,
  order): about +0.06.
- Other English words with a leading space: about -0.004. Everything else: 0.

Why: the component's activation is small (std 0.035) and mostly driven by which token it is.
This sketch captures the broad sign pattern, not the individual large spikes.
"""
READS = ()

# Degree and universality words: the component goes clearly negative on these.
DEGREE_WORDS = {
    "always", "ever", "once", "everything", "everyone", "everybody", "anything",
    "thing", "maximum", "minimum", "possible", "impossible", "highly", "extremely",
    "easily", "variety", "double", "free", "less",
}
# Mildly positive English words.
SOFT_WORDS = {"again", "simply", "quite", "various", "full", "least", "while", "order"}


def _is_han(ch):
    return "一" <= ch <= "鿿"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip().lower()
    if tok and _is_han(tok[0]):
        value = -0.03
    elif word in DEGREE_WORDS:
        value = -0.1
    elif word in SOFT_WORDS:
        value = 0.06
    elif tok.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha():
        value = -0.004
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:552 - "second word of a fixed two-word name or term".

The component fires (weakly, and only on a small fraction of tokens) on the word that
completes a fixed two-word name or technical term, once its first word has been read:
"United [States]", "New York [City]", "Space [Station]", "Northern [Ireland]",
"fiscal [year]", "Orange [County]", "Federal [Reserve]", "Homeland [Security]".

This program reads only the current token and the one before it:
  - the current word is a head word that usually ends such a name (place, government,
    organisation or technical nouns such as States, City, County, Station, Year, System);
  - the previous word starts a name: it is capitalised, or it is a modifier such as
    "fiscal" or "nuclear";
  - for a few very common names it predicts a stronger value.

Predicted activation is 0 everywhere else. Its scale was fit on about 4,000 training rows.
It explains only a small part of the variance: most of the component's activation is a
diffuse, token-specific signal that no short list of concepts captures.

READS = ()

# Nouns that often end a fixed two-word name or term.
HEAD_WORDS = frozenset({
    "States", "City", "County", "Station", "Ireland", "Korea", "Island", "Islands",
    "Power", "Year", "year", "Area", "Security", "Reserve", "Town", "Republic",
    "Conference", "Engineering", "System", "Force", "Government", "Library",
    "Headquarters", "Online", "Park", "Energy", "University", "Union", "Court",
    "Office", "Department", "Party", "Army", "Navy", "Council", "Bank", "Service",
    "Records", "Assembly", "Sheriff", "Kingdom", "Africa", "Coast", "Guard",
    "Hospital", "School", "College", "Institute", "Center", "Company", "Corporation",
    "Agency", "Commission", "Committee", "Board", "Ministry", "reactor", "plant",
})

# Words that start a name even when they are not capitalised.
NAME_STARTERS = frozenset({"fiscal", "nuclear", "solar", "federal", "national"})

# Very common names, which get a stronger prediction.
STRONG_PAIRS = frozenset({
    ("United", "States"), ("York", "City"), ("Space", "Station"),
    ("Fiscal", "Year"), ("fiscal", "year"), ("Northern", "Ireland"),
    ("South", "Korea"), ("Power", "Station"),
})

    """Activation at the newest token: a name-completing head word gets a value."""
    words = prefix.token_strings

        return None, 0.0

Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:553 is silent almost everywhere: on ordinary text its
activation stays within about 0.1 of zero. It fires on numbers written at the very start
of a document (position 0 after a document break, where attention has no earlier context):

- a digit as the document's first token: a large activation, about 4.4
  (the digits range from about 3.2 for "0" to about 5.5 for "2");
- a digit as the document's second token, when the first token was also a digit (the
  document opens with a number): a medium activation, about 1.2;
- any other token, or any digit later in a document: about 0.

Documents are the runs of equal document ids in a packed row; positions restart at each one,
as the model's own positions do.
"""

READS = ()

DIGITS = set("0123456789")
FIRST_DIGIT = 4.4
SECOND_DIGIT = 1.2


def _opens_document(document_ids, i):
    return i == 0 or document_ids[i] != document_ids[i - 1]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if strings[t] not in DIGITS:
        return None, 0.0
    if _opens_document(docs, t):
        return None, FIRST_DIGIT
    if t >= 1 and _opens_document(docs, t - 1) and strings[t - 1] in DIGITS:
        return None, SECOND_DIGIT
    return None, 0.0

"""Short word openings in likely non-English Latin-script text.

Decaying counts of function words and accented letters estimate language
context. Short ASCII word openings tend to receive larger positive values.
Case, word endings, initial whitespace, and function-word class adjust the
response. Other tokens return zero. State resets whenever the document label changes.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import unicodedata

READS = ()

ENGLISH_FUNCTION = frozenset("""

both but by can could did do does each every for from had has have he her
here his how i if in into is it its just many may might more most much must
no not now of on only or other our out over she should so some such than
that the their then there these they this those through to under up very
was we were what when where which who will with would you your
""".split())

FRENCH = frozenset("""

l la le les leur leurs mais nous ont ou où par pas pour qu que qui son sont
sur tous tout un une vous à être
""".split())

dieser dieses doch dort du durch ein eine einem einen einer eines er es
etwas hat hatte hier ich ihm ihnen ihr ihren immer ist kann kein keine mehr
mit nach nicht noch nur oder ohne sehr sein seine seiner seit sich sie sind
und vom von vor war weil wenn werden wie wir wird wäre zu zum zur über
""".split())

ITALIAN = frozenset("""
al alla alle anche che come con da dei del della delle di e gli ha il lo
nel nella non si sono sul una uno
""".split())

IBERIAN = frozenset("""
al ao com como con das de del do dos el em es foi la las los muy más na nos
não o os para pela pelo pero por que sin sobre sus são um uma un una y
""".split())

# Iberian here means common Spanish and Portuguese function words.
LANGUAGES = (FRENCH, GERMAN, ITALIAN, IBERIAN)
FOREIGN_FUNCTION = frozenset().union(*LANGUAGES)
CUES = tuple(words - frozenset().union(
    *(LANGUAGES[j] for j in range(4) if j != i))
    for i, words in enumerate(LANGUAGES))
FOREIGN_EVIDENCE = (FOREIGN_FUNCTION - ENGLISH_FUNCTION
    - {'qu', 'l'}) | frozenset("""
aan adalah akan aki ale am att av az bir bu byl care co csak cu daha dalam
dan dari dat dengan det deze değil din dit een egy este för han har het
hogy hun ile im ini inte itu için ja jag jak je jest juga kan lui maar med
naar ne nem nie niet nu och od og olan olarak om ook op pada per po pro
przez på se się som su sunt tak te tidak til untuk van ve voor wordt yang
za zijn är çok és že și
""".split())

@lru_cache(maxsize=160000)
def spelling(token):
    word = token.strip()
    latin = bool(word) and all(
        ch.isalpha() and 'LATIN' in unicodedata.name(ch, '') for ch in word)
    return word, word.lower(), latin


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = int(prefix.document_ids[-1])
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        foreign, english, previous, languages = 0., 0., '', [0.]*4
    else:
        _, foreign, english, previous, languages = carry
    word, low, latin = spelling(token)
    spaced = bool(token[:1].isspace())
    bare = not spaced and (not previous or previous[-1:].isspace())
    opening = latin and (spaced or bare)
    accented = latin and not word.isascii()

    # Recent language cues, with an approximately twenty-token memory.
    foreign *= .95
    english *= .95
    if opening:
        foreign += low in FOREIGN_EVIDENCE
        english += low in ENGLISH_FUNCTION and low not in FOREIGN_FUNCTION
    foreign += 1.2 * accented

    languages = [.95 * a + float(opening and low in cues)
                 for a, cues in zip(languages, CUES)]

    if function_word:

            + 0.212 * word.istitle())

        value += -0.097 + strength * 0.145

        gain += -0.412 * low.endswith('en')
        gain += -0.109 * low.endswith('er')
        gain += -0.023 * low.endswith('ed')
        gain += -0.238 * low.endswith('ing')
        gain += -0.1 * low.endswith('tion')
        gain += 0.07 * low.endswith('ment')
        gain += -0.292 * low.endswith('ly')

"""Short Latin word-opening fragments in non-English-looking text (layer 0, MLP down_proj, component 554).

The component is positive on a token that opens a word (it has a leading space), is a
short run of Latin letters, and is not itself a common word: the first piece of a longer
word the tokenizer split, such as " pr" (prisms, prevent), " ver", " sk", " fr", " Com",
or a lone " d" / " k". Complete words (" the", " river", " again") and non-Latin words
stay near zero.

The same fragments fire strongly in Czech, Italian, Hungarian or German text but are
mostly silent inside English prose or code. So the program keeps a running count of how
many words of the current document are common English function words, and only predicts
the fragment when that share is small.

Prediction: about 0.25 for a fragment in a non-English document, 0 elsewhere.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Common English words: a token that is one of these is a whole word, and a document
# full of them is English text.
COMMON_WORDS = frozenset(
    """a an and are as at be but by can do for from had has have he her his i if in
    is it its me my no not of on or our out she so that the their them then there
    they this to up us was we were what when which who will with would you your
    about all also any been before both can could did each more most much must
    other over some such than these those through time two one new first only
    into just like make may new many people said see some get take use work
    part set number year good way world life day know think come people world group state system home school city country company government public information university national business report house service data during around under between still while where should during every money again never always often book read write made find found give gave tell told place end same different next last early late high long small large great little old young hand head eye water land night night morning light house door family friend friends child children man woman men women play game line point case fact problem question side area money story thing things right left open close start end help keep let put run""".split()
)

LATIN_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]+")
MAX_LEN = 4           # longest fragment, in letters
ENGLISH_SHARE = 0.15  # documents with more common English words than this are English
LEVEL = 0.25          # predicted activation for a fragment


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, words so far in it, common English words so far in it).
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, 0)
    _, seen, english = carry

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    opens_word = token[:1].isspace()
    is_fragment = (
        opens_word
        and LATIN_WORD.fullmatch(word) is not None
        and len(word) <= MAX_LEN
        and word not in COMMON_WORDS
    )
    share = english / seen if seen else 0.0
    value = LEVEL if is_fragment and share < ENGLISH_SHARE else 0.0

    # Count this token for the tokens after it.
    carry = (doc, seen + 1, english + (word in COMMON_WORDS))
    return carry, value

somewhat stronger cue. This is only a weak lexical-boundary heuristic, not a
recognizer of the many particular words that also influence the component.

FUNCTION_WORDS = {
    "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "been", "but", "by",
    "de", "der", "des", "die", "ein", "eine", "et", "for", "from",
    "in", "is", "it", "la", "le", "les", "of", "on", "or", "the",
    "to", "und", "un", "une", "von", "was", "with",

SHRINK = 0.331

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.lstrip()
    if not word or not word[0].isalpha():
        return None, BASE

    docs = prefix.document_ids
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    starts_word = token[:1].isspace() or new_document

        previous = prefix.text_prefixes[-2] if prefix.position else ""

            previous and (previous[-1].isspace() or not previous[-1].isalnum())
        )

    if not starts_word or word.casefold() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return None, BASE

    opening = 0.16 if word[0].isupper() else 0.08
    return None, BASE + SHRINK * opening
